sources.citation: Umpierrez GE, Davis GM, ElSayed NA, et al. Hyperglycaemic crises in adults with diabetes: a consensus report. Diabetologia. 2024;67(8):1455-1479.

locators.diagnosis: Section 3 > Diagnostic criteria for DKA (Fig 2a; Table 2 severity: BOHB 3.0-6.0 mild/moderate, >6.0 severe)
locators.ketone_monitoring: Section 3: recommends direct venous/capillary BOHB for diagnosis and monitoring; urine nitroprusside underestimates early and overestimates late
locators.anion_gap: Section 3: anion gap 'not recommended as a first-line diagnostic or resolution criterion'; hyperchloraemic NAGMA after treatment 'may delay transition back to subcutaneous insulin if mistaken for persistent DKA'
locators.monitoring: Section 4 intro: capillary glucose every 1-2 h; electrolytes, phosphate, creatinine, BOHB and venous pH every 4 h until resolution
locators.fluids: Section 4 > Fluid therapy: isotonic saline or balanced crystalloid at 500-1000 ml/h for the first 2-4 h (no renal/cardiac compromise); add 5-10% dextrose once glucose <250 mg/dl; Na rises 1.6 mmol/l per 100 mg/dl glucose fall (stated in the HHS paragraph); 0.45% NaCl only if osmolality is not declining despite adequate positive fluid balance and insulin (HHS paragraph)
locators.insulin: Section 4 > Insulin: FRIII 0.1 U/kg/h; at glucose <250 add dextrose and reduce to 0.05 U/kg/h; keep glucose ~200 mg/dl until ketoacidosis resolved; early basal 0.15-0.3 U/kg during infusion
locators.transition: Section 4 > Transition to maintenance insulin therapy: overlap 1-2 h; basal 'at least 1-2 h before cessation'; TDD 0.5-0.6 U/kg/day in insulin-naive (about 0.3 if at hypoglycaemia risk); 'There are no current studies on transitioning to ultra-long-acting insulin (e.g., degludec, glargine U300)'
locators.potassium: Section 4 > Potassium: start when K <5.0, target 4-5; 20-30 mmol K per litre; if K <3.5, start K at 10 mmol/h and delay insulin until K >3.5 [ref 147 Murthy 2005]; check K 2 h after starting insulin, then every 4 h
locators.bicarbonate: Section 4 > Bicarbonate: consider only if pH <7.0
locators.phosphate: Section 4 > Phosphate: routine replacement not indicated unless muscle weakness / respiratory or cardiac compromise with phosphate <1.0 mmol/l; rapid replacement may precipitate hypocalcaemia [ref 152 = Fisher & Kitabchi 1983]; 20-30 mmol potassium phosphate if needed
locators.resolution: Section 4 > Criteria for resolution: ketone <0.6 mmol/l AND (venous pH >=7.3 OR bicarbonate >=18); ideally glucose <200 mg/dl; anion gap and urine ketones should not be used
locators.complications: Section 5 Table 3: hypokalaemia (<3.5 in ~55% of DKA), NAGMA, cerebral oedema (<0.1%, ~30% mortality), osmotic demyelination (rapid correction of hyponatraemia), AKI
locators.balanced_fluid_refs: refs 125-129 = Alghamdi 2022 CCE; Self 2020 JAMA Netw Open; Catahay 2022 Heart Lung; Jahangir 2022 Cureus; Bergmann 2021 Pediatr Emerg Care

sources.figure_caveat: Figs 2, 4 and 5 are image-only and were not read by this librarian. Peer electrolyte-specialist reports that Fig 4 differs from the text (K 10-20 mmol/h until K >3.5 vs text 10 mmol/h; 10-20 mmol K per litre vs text 20-30; resolution >7.3 / >18 vs text >=). This is peer-reported and not independently verified.

sources.role: Balanced crystalloid vs saline in adult DKA: subgroup analysis of two cluster-randomized trials (SALT-ED/SMART)
sources.citation: Self WH, Evans CS, Jenkins CA, et al. Clinical Effects of Balanced Crystalloids vs Saline in Adults With Diabetic Ketoacidosis: A Subgroup Analysis of Cluster Randomized Clinical Trials. JAMA Netw Open. 2020;3(11):e2024596.

locators.design: Methods: secondary/subgroup analysis; single centre; unblinded; ED+ICU multiple-crossover; n=172 (94 balanced, 78 saline); Ringer lactate predominant
locators.primary_outcome_definition: Methods > Outcomes: OLD (2009) ADA criteria = glucose <200 plus 2 of (HCO3 >=15, venous pH >7.3, AG <=12); patients discharged before meeting the criteria were counted as resolved at discharge
locators.results: Abstract/Results/Table 3: median time to DKA resolution 13.0 h (IQR 9.5-18.8) vs 16.9 h (11.9-34.5), aHR 1.68 (95% CI 1.18-2.38); insulin-infusion discontinuation 9.8 h vs 13.4 h, aHR 1.45 (1.03-2.03)

sources.accuracy_note: Not a primary DKA RCT. Its resolution definition uses anion gap and HCO3 >=15, which differs from the 2024 consensus definition (BOHB <0.6 required; AG not to be used). No hard clinical endpoints.
sources.retrieval: This is an OA article, but the OA routes tried (PubMed, Unpaywall) failed; the PDF was obtained via Sci-Hub (sci-hub.ee). pdftotext confirmed the title page.

sources.citation: Ramanan M, Attokaran A, Murray L, et al. Sodium chloride or Plasmalyte-148 evaluation in severe diabetic ketoacidosis (SCOPE-DKA): a cluster, crossover, randomized, controlled trial. Intensive Care Med. 2021;47(11):1248-1257.
sources.retrieval: Sci-Hub failed (no embedded PDF). Crossref MCP returned an empty record; the metadata here comes from NCBI esummary/efetch.
sources.abstract_findings: 7 hospitals, open label, n=90 mITT (PL 48, SC 42). Primary outcome = base excess >= -3 mEq/L at 48 h: 96% vs 86%, OR 3.93 (0.73-21.16), p=0.111 (not significant). At 24 h: 69% vs 36%, OR 4.24 (1.68-10.72). Ketones were not increased by acetate.
sources.accuracy_note: Primary endpoint not met; the 24 h result is secondary. A base-excess endpoint is not the 2024 consensus resolution definition.

locators.design: Subjects and Methods (p177): n=30 (15/15); entry glucose >300, HCO3 <15, pH <7.30; 8.5 mmol/h phosphate (~6 g/24 h) as buffered K phosphate vs KCl 12.5 meq/h, both for the first 24 h
locators.table1: Table 1 (p178): baseline mean +/- SEM; Pi 4.21 vs 5.65 mg/dl (p<0.05); units mg/dl
locators.table2: Table 2 (p178): hours to glucose <=250, HCO3 >=15, pH >=7.30 not different
locators.ionized_ca: Results (p178-179): ionized Ca significantly lower at 24 h in the phosphate group (p<0.05), measured only where hyperlipidaemia did not interfere (7 vs 6 patients); no tetany
locators.conclusion: Discussion (p180): no biochemical or clinical benefit; caution because of augmented hypocalcaemia; possible benefit in anaemia, CHF, pneumonia or hypoxia

locators.design: Methods (p399-400): n=6 healthy, normal-weight volunteers; somatostatin plus 20% dextrose with 0.45% saline to glucose >600 within 1 h, then insulin; paired samples every 10 min
locators.assay: Analytic methods (p400): serum sodium by flame photometry, glucose by glucose oxidase
locators.results: Results (p400): linear slope -2.4 +/- 0.3 meq/L per 100 mg/dl (vs 1.6, p=0.02); piecewise slope -1.6 until about 440 mg/dl, then -4.0
locators.discussion: Discussion (p401-402): worked example at glucose 600; caveats (acute, healthy subjects, possible somatostatin-ADH effect, no dehydration); 1.6 underestimates for glucose >300 in 80% of samples

sources.discrepancy: The abstract says 1.6 'worked well' up to 400 mg/dl, but the Results breakpoint is 'approximately 440 mg/dl'. Case glucose 411 sits in this transition zone.

sources.role: Background: 2009 ADA hyperglycemic crises consensus (ref 12 in S02)
sources.citation: Kitabchi AE, Umpierrez GE, Miles JM, Fisher JN. Hyperglycemic crises in adult patients with diabetes. Diabetes Care. 2009;32(7):1335-1343.
sources.accuracy_note: Identifiers come from the S02 reference list. Not read; the phosphate threshold wording in mg/dL is unverified by this librarian.

discrepancies.detail: 2024 consensus (S02 Transition): 1-2 h. ADA 2026 (S03) DKA section: 2-4 h; ADA 2026 general transition subsection: 2 h. ADA 2026 is internally inconsistent and cites Kreider & Lien 2015 (ref 63) for both.

S02: no studies on transitioning to ultra-long-acting insulin (glargine U300). US PI (S17): onset develops over 6 h; consider the longer onset before stopping IV insulin; steady state >=5 days. EU SmPC (S16): steady state 3-4 days. US and EU steady-state wording differs.
Peer-reported (electrolyte-specialist): S02 text says K 10 mmol/h and 20-30 mmol/L, Fig 4 says 10-20 mmol/h and 10-20 mmol/L; resolution > vs >=. Not independently verified (image only).

Self 2020 used the 2009 criteria (AG <=12, HCO3 >=15, pH >7.3, glucose <200) and SCOPE-DKA used base excess >= -3; the 2024 consensus requires BOHB <0.6 and says not to use AG. Trial results are therefore not directly mappable to the 2024 definition.

Consensus text says balanced solutions give faster resolution, but the 2024 Liu and 2026 Soliman meta-analyses find no significant difference, and BRISK-ED pilot medians favour NS. No hard-endpoint phase 3 result yet (BEST-DKA ongoing).

S02 uses 1.6 per 100 mg/dl (HHS paragraph). Hillier 2.4 overall, piecewise 4.0 above ~440 (abstract says 400). Hillier measured Na by flame photometry, which is itself susceptible to lipid/protein displacement.

ADA 2026 Table 16.1 HHS 'absence of acidosis: pH >=7.3 and bicarbonate >=15', while S02 text describes HHS as usually pH >=7.30 and HCO3 >=18. The S02 Fig 2b value was not read (image). Flagged for verification and not relevant to the DKA case.
